routes.label: Express both complements using one angle

question: If \(\angle A\) is four times \(\angle B,\) and the complement of \(\angle B\) is four times the complement of \(\angle A,\) then \(\angle B=\)
solution:
A complement has measure \(90^\circ\) minus the original angle, so expressing both angles using one unknown gives a single equation. Let \(x\) be the degree measure of \(\angle B\). Then \(\angle A\) has degree measure \(4x\), and the complement condition becomes
\[
90-x=4(90-4x).
\]
Expanding and collecting terms gives
\[
90-x=360-16x,
\qquad 15x=270,
\qquad x=18.
\]
Then \(\angle A=72^\circ\). Their complements are \(72^\circ\) and \(18^\circ\), respectively, so both stated four-to-one relationships hold. Therefore \(\boxed{\angle B=18^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
